title: Universally closed stack diagonals descend through universal homeomorphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\mathcal Z/k$ an algebraic stack, $Q/k$ an algebraic space, and $f:\mathcal Z\to Q$ a universal homeomorphism. Assume that $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/k}:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z$ is universally closed: after every algebraic-stack base change, its map of point spaces is closed. Then $\Delta_{Q/k}:Q\to Q\times_kQ$ is a closed immersion, so $Q$ is separated over $k$. Here a universal homeomorphism means a homeomorphism on point spaces after every algebraic-stack base change. Point spaces are field-valued objects modulo isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by smooth scheme atlases. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces means a closed immersion after scheme charts [def-weil-closed-immersion]. No finiteness-of-inertia, finite-type or adequacy hypothesis is assumed on $f$. Algebraic stacks and spaces use [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 0DUY (lemma-keel-mori-diagonal), proof for separatedness, with the same argument applied over k to any universal homeomorphism with universally closed source diagonal; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04Y0 (lemma-separated-diagonal-proper), equivalence of universal closedness of an algebraic-space diagonal with its being a closed immersion.

proof.text: Use the algebraic-stack 2-fibre products of [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Factor $f\times f$ as $\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z\xrightarrow{f\times1}Q\times_k\mathcal Z\xrightarrow{1\times f}Q\times_kQ$. Each factor is a base change of $f$. After any further algebraic-stack base change, its point map is therefore a homeomorphism by the hypothesis on $f$. The point map of the base-changed composite is the composite of these two homeomorphisms (factor the base change through the intermediate stack), so $f\times f$ is a universal homeomorphism. Functoriality of point maps is immediate on field-valued representatives; their topologies are those of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 0DUY (lemma-keel-mori-diagonal), separatedness argument, applied over k; universal homeomorphisms as in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: Let $T\to Q\times_kQ$ be any algebraic-space morphism, and set $D=Q\times_{Q\times_kQ}T$, $B=(\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z)\times_{Q\times_kQ}T$, and $A=\mathcal Z\times_{Q\times_kQ}T$, where the last structure map is $(f,f)$. These are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]; $D$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The equality $(f\times f)\Delta_{\mathcal Z}=\Delta_Qf$ gives a commutative square with top map $a:A\to B$, bottom map $d:D\to T$ and vertical maps $u:A\to D$, $v:B\to T$. Associating the 2-fibre products identifies $A$ with $\mathcal Z\times_QD$ and also with $\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z}B$: both identifications just retain the same object of $\mathcal Z$, point of $T$, and the two isomorphisms in the product. Thus $u$ is a base change of $f$, $v$ of $f\times f$, and $a$ of $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/k}$. Consequently $|u|,|v|$ are homeomorphisms and $|a|$ is closed by the hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0DUY (lemma-keel-mori-diagonal), separatedness argument, applied over k; universal homeomorphisms as in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: For a closed subset $C\subseteq|D|$, the subset $|u|^{-1}(C)$ is closed in $|A|$. Its image under $|a|$ is closed in $|B|$, and its image under the homeomorphism $|v|$ is closed in $|T|$. Commutativity on field-valued points and surjectivity of $|u|$ give the exact equality $|d|(C)=|v|\bigl(|a|(|u|^{-1}(C))\bigr)$. Hence $|d|$ is closed. The point topologies agree with the usual algebraic-space topologies by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. As $T$ was arbitrary, $\Delta_{Q/k}$ is universally closed in the algebraic-space sense.

source.place: Tag 0DUY (lemma-keel-mori-diagonal), separatedness argument, applied over k; universal homeomorphisms as in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] with base scheme $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $U=Q$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g$ the structure morphism. Its diagonal is $\Delta_{Q/k}$. Step 3 tested every algebraic-space base change $T\to Q\times_kQ$ and proved its point map closed, with precisely the etale-atlas topology required by the cited statement. Thus that statement makes $\Delta_{Q/k}$ a representable map whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes; this is its explicit meaning of a closed immersion of algebraic spaces. Hence $Q/k$ is separated. The criterion requires neither quasi-compactness nor finite type of $g$.
